title: Interaction effects on Andreev states from an electromagnetic environment
authors: Erik S. Samuelsen, Yuli V. Nazarov
abstract: Here we present a detailed theoretical investigation of the environment-induced interaction correction to the ground states and addition energies in a short superconducting junction. We derive general formulas for these corrections linking them to the frequency-dependent admittance of the junction and the environment impedance. We specify two environmental models: that of an external impedance and the Mattis-Bardeen model. In both cases we assume $G_Q Z \ll 1$, where $G_Q$ is the conductance quantum and $Z$ the typical environmental resistance.   While an expectation is that the typical scale of the relative correction is of the order $G_Q Z$, we have found that in many cases the dimensionless scale $L G_Q Δ$ provides a better estimation, where $Δ$ is the superconducting energy gap and $L$ an external inductance. We discuss the logarithmic renormalizations of the energies by low- and high-frequency phase fluctuations and single out a non-superconducting contribution related to the renormalization of transmission eigenvalues. We investigate in detail the peculiarities of the corrections at: i. small phases, where the interaction causes a current jump, ii. Andreev bound state energies close to the gap edge, iii. Andreev bound state energies close to Fermi level. In all these cases the correction may become comparable with the unperturbed energy, even for $G_Q Z \ll 1$, and we briefly sketch non-perturbative models relevant for the situations.
summary: This theoretical study calculates the interaction corrections to the energy levels of a superconducting junction due to coupling with an electromagnetic environment. By employing advanced techniques like the Keldysh formalism and diagrammatic expansions, the authors derive formulas showing that these environmental effects can significantly alter superconducting properties, even when the coupling appears weak.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates how coupling a short superconducting junction to an electromagnetic environment modifies the ground state energies and addition energies of its Andreev bound states.
main_result: The interaction corrections are derived, showing that the relative correction scale can be governed by $L G_Q \Delta$ rather than the naive $G_Q Z$, and these corrections can be significant even when the coupling strength $G_Q Z$ is small.
method: The authors use a theoretical framework involving the calculation of junction admittance via the Keldysh technique and diagrammatic expansion (Feynman diagrams) to account for environmental coupling.
model_or_system: The system is a short superconducting junction connecting two superconductors, whose energy levels (Andreev bound states) are perturbed by an external electromagnetic environment modeled either by an external impedance or the Mattis-Bardeen model.
key_observables: Interaction corrections to the even ground state energy ($\Delta E(e)$), the odd doublet addition energy ($\delta_{	ext{odd}}$), and the singlet addition energy ($\delta_{	ext{even}}$).
important_parameters: Superconducting energy gap ($\Delta$), conductance quantum ($G_Q$), environmental impedance ($Z$), external inductance ($L$), and various frequency scales ($\omega_H, \omega_L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the junction is 'short' and employs approximations based on the relative strength of coupling ($G_Q Z \ll 1$), while also exploring non-perturbative regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup, the impedance models for the environment, and the decomposition of the state-resolved junction admittance as a function of frequency.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the physical system and environmental models, deriving general formulas for interaction corrections, calculating specific energy shifts ($\Delta E_e, \delta_{	ext{odd}}, \delta_{	ext{even}}$) using diagrammatic techniques, and analyzing the results in various physical regimes (small phases, near gap edges).
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum electrodynamics in condensed matter, as it provides quantitative predictions for how environmental dissipation and coupling modify fundamental superconducting quantum properties.
